subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord multi-agent preflight suppress the current/default route whenever the opening attention context targets another configured OpenClaw bot, role, or reply target?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but strict active-target semantics alter stable Discord routing and default-owner behavior in existing multi-bot deployments.

options.title: Adopt Strict Active Targeting
options.body: Implement mention/reply/role target selection before default routing, suppress non-target agents, and add tests for opening attention, quoted/later mentions, other-agent targeting, and bot-loop cases.

options.title: Keep Default Owner Unless Opted In
options.body: Preserve current default-owner behavior and introduce an explicit Discord policy surface for strict multi-bot suppression only after config/API approval.

options.title: Resolve Narrow Trackers First
options.body: Handle default-owner precedence, role triggers, slash-command targeting, and bot-authored reply policy through their separate canonical items before closing or narrowing this broad report.

recommendation.title: Adopt Strict Active Targeting
recommendation.body: Implement mention/reply/role target selection before default routing, suppress non-target agents, and add tests for opening attention, quoted/later mentions, other-agent targeting, and bot-loop cases.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest code-history and prior-review signal for Discord mention policy, route resolution, and the compatibility decision.
